row.subject: hanson-1998-is-a-singularity-just-around-the-corner
row.statement: Hanson’s article “Is a Singularity Just Around the Corner?” (Journal of Transhumanism, June 1998) says that if the rate of improvement in any one input consistently lags behind the rest, that input becomes a bottleneck limiting the growth rate of the entire process; the next paragraph names the training of professionals who understand computing and its applications as such a bottleneck.

time.note: Page heading “Journal of Transhumanism 2, June 1998”; no day printed.

row.qualification: A constraint from uneven improvement in essential inputs; it does not say that all automation must be absent. In the article, faster and cheaper hardware alone does not remove the bottleneck it names. Earliest located means the earliest text found by the collection’s searches, the cross-family re-check of 2026-11-02 and the archive retrieval of 2026-11-02, not a first statement.
